description_medium: Starting March 16, 2025, the Trump administration began paying El Salvador $20,000 per inmate per year to house U.S. deportees in CECOT, the Terrorism Confinement Center, a maximum-security facility where inmates have their heads shaved, are kept in communal cells of up to 100 men for 23.5 hours per day on metal bunks with no mattresses, with no visitation, education, or recreation permitted.
description_long: The supplied record describes the event and its immediate context. Starting March 16, 2025, the Trump administration began paying El Salvador $20,000 per inmate per year to house U.S. deportees in CECOT, the Terrorism Confinement Center, a maximum-security facility where inmates have their heads shaved, are kept in communal cells of up to 100 men for 23.5 hours per day on metal bunks with no mattresses, with no visitation, education, or recreation permitted. Human rights organizations condemned the arrangement as a potential violation of international law's non-refoulement principle and the Convention Against Torture. By July 2025, El Salvador acknowledged to UN investigators that the Trump administration maintained 'exclusive jurisdiction and legal responsibility' over the CECOT detainees. At least 101 of the 261 initial deportees had no alleged gang ties, having been sent there simply for being in the U.S. without documentation. title: Article 5 Doubt: Trump Publicly Questions NATO's Mutual Defense Guarantee Before Hague Summit
description_short: Article 5 Doubt: Trump Publicly Questions NATO's Mutual Defense Guarantee Before Hague Summit
description_medium: On June 24, 2025, while flying to the NATO summit in the Netherlands, Trump publicly cast doubt on whether the United States would honor Article 5 — the alliance's core mutual defense commitment — telling reporters there were numerous definitions of the clause. The statement alarmed allies already unsettled by months of US hostility.
description_long: The supplied record describes the event and its immediate context. On June 24, 2025, while flying to the NATO summit in the Netherlands, Trump publicly cast doubt on whether the United States would honor Article 5 — the alliance's core mutual defense commitment — telling reporters there were numerous definitions of the clause. The statement alarmed allies already unsettled by months of US hostility. Though Trump eventually reaffirmed a nominal Article 5 commitment at the summit and secured a new 5% GDP defense spending target, the New York Times reported the summit's language was deliberately mushy, pledging that allies — not all allies — would meet the target. Spain formally opted out. A Reuters summary noted the event was tailor-made to placate Trump. The episode gave Putin a strategic gift, confirming European fears that Washington's security guarantee was transactional and unreliable.
